subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should literal `openai` auto fallback session route state be owned by the OpenAI provider doctor contract, by the Codex doctor contract, or by provider-agnostic auto-fallback cleanup?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but `openai` is the canonical OpenAI provider id and also part of the Codex app-server routing story, so automation should not pick the permanent ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add an OpenAI doctor owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and keep Codex focused on legacy Codex ids and runtime names while testing auto fallback cleanup versus explicit OpenAI pins.

options.title: Codex owns OpenAI app-server route state
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex owner if maintainers define Codex doctor cleanup as responsible for OpenAI/Codex app-server route pins.

options.title: Make auto fallback cleanup provider-agnostic
options.body: Have doctor clear stale automatic session route overrides by comparing configured route and fallback origin without requiring plugin ownership for canonical provider ids.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add an OpenAI doctor owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and keep Codex focused on legacy Codex ids and runtime names while testing auto fallback cleanup versus explicit OpenAI pins.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged session route-state doctor repair and the nearest follow-up Codex session repair, so he has the strongest history for this boundary choice.
